1	# Archive Jira Ticket to CB-Full-Feature
2	
3	Archive a Jira ticket's feature requirements into the Cookbook Full Features Detail Requirements documentation (`Z01-Resource/CB-full-feature/`). This is a personal workflow for Bonnie's Wonder Cookbook documentation maintenance.
4	
5	## Language
6	
7	**All documentation updates must be in English.** Page content, Change Log tables, new pages — everything written into CB-full-feature is English-only.
8	
9	## Target Directory
10	
11	**`Z01-Resource/CB-full-feature/`** — the dedicated directory for all Cookbook feature requirement pages (mirrored from Confluence space RT).
12	
13	## When to Use
14	
15	- User provides a Jira ticket link (e.g., MD-XXXXX) and asks to integrate its requirements into CB-full-feature
16	- User says "archive ticket to CB", "integrate into full feature docs", or similar
17	
18	## Workflow
19	
20	### Step 1: Read the Ticket
21	
22	Fetch the full Jira ticket via Atlassian MCP tools (`jira_get_issue` with `fields=*all`). Capture:
23	- Summary, description, acceptance criteria
24	- All comments (especially implementation summaries and clarifications)
25	- Linked Confluence pages or Figma references
26	- **Always read the latest ticket description** — it is the authoritative source. Comments may contain outdated discussions.
27	
28	### Step 2: Explore the Documentation — Read EVERY Page
29	
30	**Do not skip any page.** You must read the full content of every single `.md` file in `Z01-Resource/CB-full-feature/` and all its sub-directories. This is not optional — a requirement buried in an unexpected page will be missed if you only read "related" pages.
31	
32	1. **Enumerate all files**: Use `find Z01-Resource/CB-full-feature -name "*.md" | sort` to get the complete file list.
33	2. **Read the overview pages first**:
34	   - `README.md`
35	   - `Cookbook Full Features Detail Requirements.md` (the summary index)
36	3. **Read every sub-directory page, without exception**:
37	   - `01 Fields & Cards in Items.md`
38	   - Every page under `02Common Features/` (including `Backend Features/` sub-directory)
39	   - Every page under `Item Details/` (including all sub-directories like `Components/`, `Nutritions/`, `Procedure Card/`, `Item Information/`, `Hot Holding Card/`, `Customization V2/`, `Usages/`, etc.)
40	   - Every page under `Item Grid/`
41	   - Every page under `Configurations/` (including `Locations/` sub-directory)
42	   - Every page under `Menu/`
43	   - Every page under `Line Build/`
44	   - Every page under `Benchtop Recipe/`
45	   - Every page under `Variant-Test Kitchen/`
46	   - Every page under `WSKUs & Consumables Grid/`
47	   - Every page under `Vendor Items/`
48	   - Every page under `Features TBD/` (including `Create Item/Create Ingredient/` sub-directory)
49	   - `HDR Consumable Item 40 Detail.md`
50	   - `Scheduled changes.md`
51	   - `User List.md`
52	4. **Compare each page against the ticket**: After reading each page, ask: does this page intersect with any requirement in the ticket? If yes, flag it for potential modification. If no, explicitly note it as "no change needed."
53	5. **Pay extra attention to cross-cutting concerns** that span multiple pages:
54	   - A new card → affects Fields & Cards matrix, the card's own detail page, validations, publish flow, copy/version creation, change history, and compare change history
55	   - A validation rule change → may affect both the validations page and the publish workflow page
56	   - A field behavior change → may affect the card's detail page and the item grid page
57	
58	**The goal**: after this step, you should have read every page and be able to state — for *each* page — why it does or does not need changes.
59	
60	### Step 3: Analyze & Plan (internal)
61	
62	Map ticket requirements to documentation pages. For each page, determine:
63	- **Modify existing page** — what exact content to add/change
64	- **Create new page** — what the page should contain
65	- **No change needed** — pages that are unaffected (track internally for completeness; do NOT include in user review)
66	
67	### Step 4: Present Plan for Review (DO NOT EXECUTE YET)
68	
69	Present a structured plan showing **only pages that need changes** (modify or create):
70	
71	- **Before** — the current content (exact excerpt)
72	- **After** — the proposed new content
73	- **Rationale** — why this change is needed
74	
75	**Do NOT list pages that need no changes** — they add noise without value for review. If the user asks whether a specific page was checked, answer directly.
76	
77	**Critical: Wait for user approval before making ANY edits.**
78	
79	### Step 5: Execute After Approval
80	
81	Only after the user explicitly approves (item by item or all at once), execute the changes.
82	
83	## Editing Conventions
84	
85	### Change Log Table
86	
87	**Every modified page MUST have a Change Log table at the bottom** tracking the update:
88	
89	```markdown
90	---
91	
92	## Change Log
93	
94	| Version | Date | Updated By | Description |
95	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
96	| 1.0 | YYYY-MM-DD | System | Initial fetch from Confluence |
97	| 1.1 | YYYY-MM-DD | Bonnie Yang | [MD-XXXXX](https://wonder.atlassian.net/browse/MD-XXXXX) — Brief description of what was changed. |
98	```
99	
100	- If the page already has a Change Log, append a new row
101	- If the page doesn't have one, add the full table (including the initial fetch row)
102	- Date format: `YYYY-MM-DD`
103	- Ticket link must be a clickable markdown link to the Jira issue
104	
105	### Page Content Rules
106	
107	- **All content in English**
108	- **Do NOT delete pages** — only modify or create
109	- **Do NOT modify unrelated content** — stay focused on the ticket's scope
110	- **Do NOT duplicate content** across pages — if a topic is already documented in its dedicated page, use a brief cross-reference wikilink instead of repeating it
111	- Use `[[wikilinks]]` for internal references between CB-full-feature pages
112	- Preserve existing frontmatter, images, and formatting
113	
114	### Section Numbering
115	
116	- Insert new sections with sequential numbering
117	- When adding a section between existing ones, shift subsequent section numbers
118	- Peer-level features get their own top-level section number (not a sub-section of another feature)
119	
120	### Validation Levels
121	
122	Pay close attention to whether a validation is:
123	- **required** / **error** — blocks publishing
124	- **warning** / **optional** — shows warning but allows "Publish Anyway"
125	
126	The ticket description is the authoritative source. Cross-check against comments — if there's a conflict, the ticket description wins.
127	
128	### Cross-References
129	
130	When a topic spans multiple pages:
131	- Write the full detail in the most relevant dedicated page
132	- Other pages reference it with a brief wikilink + one-line summary
133	- Example: Missing Info validation details go in `Item Validations-Missing Info.md`; the card page just says "See [[Item Validations-Missing Info]], section X."
134	
135	## Common Pitfalls
136	
137	1. **Assuming validation level**: Always check the ticket for "required" vs "warning". Don't copy the validation level from a similar existing feature.
138	2. **Duplicating content**: If Change History, Missing Info, or Publish behavior is already in its dedicated page, use cross-references instead of repeating.
139	3. **Wrong parent-child hierarchy**: A new card/feature is a peer of existing ones, not a child. Give it its own top-level section number.
140	4. **Forgetting Change Log tables**: Every modified page gets one at the bottom.
141	5. **Modifying unrelated pages**: Only touch pages directly affected by the ticket.
142	6. **Editing before approval**: Never modify files until the user explicitly approves the plan.
143	
144	## Quick Reference
145	
146	| Task | Tool |
147	|------|------|
148	| Read Jira ticket | `mcp__mcp-atlassian__jira_get_issue` |
149	| List CB-full-feature files | `find Z01-Resource/CB-full-feature -name "*.md"` |
150	| Read a page | `Read` tool with absolute path |
151	| Edit a page | `Edit` tool with exact `old_string` match |
152	| Create a new page | `Write` tool with full content + frontmatter |
153	| Search within files | `grep` via Bash |

24	
25	### 0. 创建 Ticket（详见 [[create-jira-ticket]] skill）

57	- `project = MD AND status = "To Do"` - 查询 MD 项目下所有 To Do

7	
8	You MUST follow these conventions when creating or modifying any note in this vault.

10	## Pre-Flight Checklist
11	
12	Before creating any note:
13	
14	1. Read `AGENTS.md` — check the knowledge base structure (user notes vs agent-maintained pages)

17	
18	## Creating Notes
19	
20	Prefer `obsidian create` when Obsidian is running (it keeps the wikilink graph
21	consistent):
22	
23	```
24	obsidian create name="Note Title" content="<frontmatter + content>" silent
25	```
26	
27	For multiline content use `\n` for newline and `\t` for tab.
28	
29	In headless environments (Obsidian closed, CLI-initialized workspaces), write the
30	`.md` file directly with identical frontmatter and naming conventions, and run
31	`knowlery health` after bulk changes.
32	
33	## Required Frontmatter
34	
35	Every note MUST have these fields:
36	
37	| Field | Values |
38	|-------|--------|
39	| `title` | Descriptive title |
40	| `type` | `meeting`, `idea`, `reference`, `daily`, `project`, `person`, `entity`, `concept`, `comparison`, `query`, etc. |
41	| `date` | YYYY-MM-DD — today's date or extracted from content |
42	| `tags` | Array of relevant tags |

49	| `references` | Related notes as wikilinks: `[[Note Name]]` |
50	| `status` | `draft`, `active`, `completed`, `archived` |
51	| `updated` | YYYY-MM-DD — last substantive edit (common on agent pages) |
52	| `contradictions` | Cross-links when conflicting claims need review (agent pages) |

1	# Business Requirements Document Compilation
2	
3	Compile scattered requirements discussions from Jira tickets and Confluence pages into a structured business requirements document. The document serves as a business requirement traceability baseline for subsequent feature development.
4	
5	## Language
6	
7	**All document content must be in English**, regardless of the source material language. Source pages may be mixed Chinese/English, but the final output document is English-only.
8	
9	## Output Directory
10	
11	**`Z01-Resource/CB-business/` is the dedicated directory for all Cookbook-related business requirements documents.** All biz-req output goes here unless the user specifies a different target directory.
12	
13	## When to Use
14	
15	- User provides a Jira ticket + several Confluence reference page links
16	- User asks to write a business requirements document for a Cookbook feature
17	- Business requirements change over time and the document needs continuous iteration
18	- Default output location: `Z01-Resource/CB-business/`
19	
20	## Workflow
21	
22	### Step 1: Resource Collection
23	
24	Starting from the user-provided entry links, **exhaustively collect** all related materials:
25	
26	1. **Jira ticket**: Fetch issue content via Atlassian MCP tools. If no Jira scope is available, infer from Confluence page mentions and references.
27	2. **Confluence pages**: Fetch each page body in markdown format via `getConfluencePage` for text extraction.
28	3. **Footer comments**: `getConfluencePageFooterComments` (with replies). These often contain stakeholder alignment and design decision discussions.
29	4. **Inline comments**: `getConfluencePageInlineComments` (with replies). These often contain questions and clarifications on specific attribute values or table entries.
30	5. **Child pages**: `getConfluencePageDescendants`. Child pages may contain more granular specifications.
31	6. **Referenced pages**: Links from @mentions in body text, smartlinks, and pages mentioned in comments — fetch them if relevant to the topic.
32	7. **External resources**: Google Sheets, Figma links, etc. — fetch if publicly accessible.
33	
34	### Inaccessible Resources (CRITICAL)
35	
36	**After completing resource collection, you MUST explicitly report every resource that could not be accessed.** This is a hard requirement — do not silently skip failed fetches.
37	
38	Access failures include:
39	- Jira tickets that return 404 or authentication errors
40	- Confluence pages that return 404 or permission errors
41	- Slack links that require login / can't be fetched
42	- Google Docs/Sheets links that are private
43	- Figma links behind authentication
44	- Any URL that WebFetch cannot retrieve
45	- Footer/inline comments that fail to load
46	
47	Format the warning clearly before proceeding to Step 2:
48	```
49	⚠ Unable to access the following resources:
50	- <url1> — <reason (e.g., Confluence page not found)>
51	- <url2> — <reason (e.g., Slack login required)>
52	- <url3> — <reason (e.g., comment fetch failed)>
53	
54	The compiled document will note these as unverified references.
55	```
56	
57	**Do NOT proceed to Step 2 (Resource Analysis) until the user has seen this list.** If all resources are accessible, explicitly state: "✅ All referenced resources successfully accessed."
58	
59	### Step 2: Resource Analysis
60	
61	Perform three layers of analysis on collected materials:
62	
63	1. **Distinguish proposals vs. final decisions**: Page body content may be early drafts. Discussions in comments often contain key decision turning points. Map the timeline: who proposed what → who objected/revised → what was the final conclusion. Record rejected proposals as well (provides context for "why not").
64	2. **Identify cross-page related concepts**: The same business concept may appear across multiple pages with different framing (e.g., IK Eligible defined at component level in one page, associated with step level in another). Connect them to form a complete picture.
65	3. **Extract business rules, filter technical details**: Focus on what & why, not specific API endpoints or database fields. Technical details only retained at the "solution overview" level.
66	
67	### Step 3: Document Structure
68	
69	Organize in the following order (flexibly adapt to specific topic):
70	
71	| Section | Content |
72	|---|---|
73	| **Business Background** | Why this feature is needed, related project context |
74	| **Concept Definitions & Enum Values** | Definition, allowed values, and meaning of each core attribute |
75	| **Configuration Level** | At which level each attribute is configured (menu item / component / sub-step) and why |
76	| **Interaction Rules** | Dependencies and constraints between attributes |
77	| **Solution Design** | What each system does (overview level, not functional spec) |
78	| **Design Decision Records** | Key decision outcomes, decision makers, dates, rejected proposals and reasons |
79	| **Data Flow** | How data flows between systems |
80	| **Configuration Matrix** | Complete configuration reference for all known scenarios |
81	| **Timeline & Dependencies** | Milestones, upstream/downstream dependencies |
82	| **Open Questions** | Pending items and future iteration directions |
83	| **Reference Pages** | URL matrix of all source pages |
84	
85	### Step 4: Validation
86	
87	1. **Self-check**: Cross-reference every claim against source materials. Every claim must have a source.
88	2. **Common pitfalls to watch**:
89	   - Which level a concept applies at (component vs. step vs. menu item)
90	   - Correct data flow direction (who queries whom, who pushes to whom)
91	   - Precise meaning of "default" (system fallback vs. configuration-level inheritance)
92	   - Enum value names and counts match source materials
93	3. **Annotate sources**: Key decisions should note who decided, which page/comment, and date.
94	
95	### Step 5: Iteration
96	
97	1. Submit to stakeholder for review
98	2. Revise iteratively based on feedback until accurate
99	3. Bump `updated` date on every edit
100	4. The document is a living document — iterate as business requirements evolve
101	
102	### Step 6: Update Existing Documents
103	
104	**When updating an existing business document, do NOT modify it directly.** Instead:
105	
106	1. List the proposed changes, showing **before → after** comparisons
107	2. Submit for user review
108	3. Only execute edits after user confirms
109	
110	## Output
111	
112	A markdown document placed in `Z01-Resource/CB-business/` (the dedicated Cookbook business requirements directory), with complete frontmatter, wikilink references, and a source page URL matrix. All content in English.
113

1	# Sync Jira Ticket to Confluence
2	
3	Compare a Jira ticket with an existing Confluence page (and its child pages), identify what needs updating, present a before/after diff for review, and update only after user confirmation.
4	
5	## Input
6	
7	- **Jira ticket link** (e.g., `https://wonder.atlassian.net/browse/MD-17984`)
8	- **Confluence page link** (e.g., `https://wonder.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/MD/pages/123456789/Page+Title`)
9	
10	## Language Rule (HARD REQUIREMENT)
11	
12	**All content written to Confluence MUST be in English.** This applies to:
13	- Page titles
14	- Page body content
15	- Version comments
16	- Any labels or metadata
17	
18	When the Jira ticket description contains Chinese or other non-English content, translate it to English before writing to Confluence. Preserve the original meaning accurately.
19	
20	## Execution Steps
21	
22	### Phase 1: Fetch Source (Jira)
23	
24	1. Extract the ticket key from the Jira link
25	2. Fetch the full Jira ticket via MCP `jira_get_issue` with all fields:
26	   - Basic info: summary, status, priority, issuetype, assignee, reporter, created, updated
27	   - Description (full ADF content)
28	   - Subtasks list
29	   - Parent Epic
30	   - Issue links
31	   - Comments
32	   - Attachments (list, not download)
33	
34	### Phase 2: Fetch Target (Confluence)
35	
36	1. Extract the page ID from the Confluence link
37	2. Fetch the target page via MCP `confluence_get_page`
38	3. Fetch ALL child pages via MCP `confluence_get_page_children` (with `include_content: true`)
39	4. Build a complete content map: `{page_title: {content, page_id, parent_id}}` for the target page and every descendant
40	
41	### Phase 3: Compare & Identify Changes
42	
43	Compare Jira ticket content against the full Confluence page tree. Check for:
44	
45	| Aspect | What to check |
46	|--------|---------------|
47	| **Status** | Has the Jira status changed? Is the Confluence page reflecting the current status? |
48	| **Description** | Has the Jira description been updated? Are there new sections, changed requirements, updated AC? |
49	| **Subtasks** | New subtasks added? Existing ones completed? Status changes? |
50	| **Comments** | New comments on Jira that contain important context not yet in Confluence? |
51	| **Assignee/Reporter** | Personnel changes? |
52	| **Epic/ Links** | New parent Epic? New linked issues? |
53	| **Attachments** | New screenshots or files on Jira not in Confluence? |
54	| **Child pages** | Do child pages cover content that's now in the Jira description? Are they outdated? |
55	
56	For each change identified:
57	- Note WHICH page(s) need updating (target page or specific child page)
58	- Capture the BEFORE content (current Confluence content)
59	- Draft the AFTER content (what it should become)
60	
61	### Phase 4: Present Diff for Review
62	
63	Present findings in this format:
64	
65	```
66	## 📋 Sync Review: MD-XXXXX → Confluence
67	
68	### Pages Examined
69	- Target: [Page Title] (page_id) — last updated YYYY-MM-DD
70	- Child: [Child Page Title] (page_id)
71	- Child: [Another Child] (page_id)
72	- ... (all child pages)
73	
74	### Changes Identified: N changes across M pages
75	
76	---
77	
78	### Change 1: [Page Title] — Update Status
79	**Before:**
80	> Status: To Do
81	
82	**After:**
83	> Status: In Progress
84	
85	---
86	
87	### Change 2: [Child Page Title] — Add New Acceptance Criteria
88	**Before:**
89	> (current content or "section does not exist")
90	
91	**After:**
92	> (proposed new content in English)
93	
94	---
95	
96	### No Changes Needed
97	- [Page/Child Title] — content is up to date
98	- ...
99	
100	---
101	
102	### Summary
103	- X pages to update
104	- Y new child pages to create
105	- Z pages unchanged
106	```
107	
108	**Wait for user confirmation before proceeding to Phase 5.**
109	
110	### Phase 5: Apply Updates (after confirmation)
111	
112	For each confirmed change:
113	
114	1. **Update existing page** → MCP `confluence_update_page` with the new content
115	2. **Create new child page** → MCP `confluence_create_page` under the target parent
116	3. **Upload attachments** → MCP `confluence_upload_attachment` (if new Jira attachments found)
117	4. Each update should have a version comment like: `Synced from Jira MD-XXXXX — status update`
118	
119	### Phase 6: Report Completion
120	
121	```
122	## ✅ Sync Complete
123	
124	- Updated: [Page Title] (link) — status changed, description updated
125	- Created: [New Child Page] (link) — new section extracted
126	- Unchanged: [list pages that were already up to date]
127	```
128	
129	## Inaccessible Resources (CRITICAL)
130	
131	**If ANY step fails due to an inaccessible resource, you MUST explicitly report it to the user.** Do not proceed silently with partial data.
132	
133	| Failure | Required Action |
134	|---------|-----------------|
135	| Jira ticket not found (404) | Report: `⚠ Jira ticket <KEY> not found — verify the ticket link.` |
136	| Confluence page not found (404) | Report: `⚠ Confluence page not found — verify the page link.` |
137	| Confluence child pages fetch error | Report: `⚠ Cannot fetch child pages of <page title> — <reason>.` |
138	| Jira ticket auth error (401/403) | Report: `⚠ Cannot access Jira ticket <KEY> — authentication failed.` |
139	| Confluence create/update fails | Report: `⚠ Failed to update Confluence page <title> — <error details>.` |
140	
141	Format the warning clearly:
142	```
143	⚠ Sync encountered inaccessible resources:
144	- Jira ticket MD-XXXXX — 404 not found
145	- Child pages of "Design Doc" — permission error
146	
147	Sync halted. Please verify the links and retry.
148	```
149	
150	This is a hard requirement — never suppress or skip these notifications.
151	
152	## Ticket Content Extraction
153	
154	When fetching a Jira ticket via REST API, key fields to extract:
155	
156	| Field | API Path | Notes |
157	|-------|----------|-------|
158	| Summary | `fields.summary` | Page title candidate |
159	| Description | `fields.description` | ADF format; convert to wiki/html |
160	| Status | `fields.status.name` | |
161	| Priority | `fields.priority.name` | |
162	| Assignee | `fields.assignee.displayName` | |
163	| Reporter | `fields.reporter.displayName` | |
164	| Created | `fields.created` | |
165	| Updated | `fields.updated` | |
166	| Epic Link | `fields.parent.key` | If story has parent epic |
167	| Subtasks | `fields.subtasks[].key` | List child issues |
168	| Issue Links | `fields.issuelinks[]` | Related PRs, blocks, etc. |
169	
170	## Auth Strategy
171	
172	MCP tools are the preferred path (configured in `.claude/mcp.json`):
173	
174	- `mcp__atlassian__jira_get_issue` — fetch Jira ticket
175	- `mcp__atlassian__confluence_get_page` — fetch target page
176	- `mcp__atlassian__confluence_get_page_children` — fetch all child pages
177	- `mcp__atlassian__confluence_update_page` — update existing page
178	- `mcp__atlassian__confluence_create_page` — create new child page
179	
180	### Fallback: REST API + Cached OAuth Token
181	
182	If MCP tools for Jira are unavailable:
183	
184	```bash
185	TOKEN_FILE=$(find ~/.mcp-auth -name "8d8bab2a93ad41172215aecfb4b6d869_tokens.json" 2>/dev/null | head -1)
186	TOKEN=$(python3 -c "import json; print(json.load(open('$TOKEN_FILE'))['access_token'])")
187	CLOUD_ID="70497edc-9c59-45b2-8e47-e46913d4c6cf"
188	API="https://api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/${CLOUD_ID}/rest/api/3"
189	
190	# Fetch issue
191	curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "${API}/issue/MD-17984"
192	```
193	
194	## MCP Architecture Note
195	
196	Two config sources exist; one can shadow the other:
197	
198	| File | Config Name | Method | OAuth Scope | Jira Write |
199	|------|------------|--------|-------------|------------|
200	| `~/.claude/settings.json` | Atlassian-Rovo-MCP | mcp-remote + authv2 | Full | ✅ |
201	| `~/.claude.json` | atlassian | HTTP direct | Confluence only | ❌ |
202	
203	Confluence operations (create/update page) are available in both modes. Jira read for ticket fetching may need the REST API fallback if in HTTP-only mode.

1	# Create Jira Ticket Skill
2	
3	Create a Jira issue in the MasterData board. Analyze user-provided requirements, distill them into a well-structured Story or Task, and create it in the MD project.
4	
5	## Ticket Standards
6	
7	### Language
8	All ticket content MUST be in English — summary, description, acceptance criteria, everything.
9	
10	### Defaults
11	- **Project**: MD (MasterData) — Project Key: `MD`, System ID: `10024`
12	  - Board: [MD Board](https://wonder.atlassian.net/jira/software/c/projects/MD/boards/10)
13	  - Note: `10024` is the internal Jira project ID used in REST API calls, NOT a ticket number. Ticket numbers (e.g., MD-17984) are auto-generated by Jira on creation.
14	  - **Always use MD.** Never use MDD — it only has Task/Epic/Subtask, no Story type.
15	- **Assignee**: bonnieyang@xm.wonder.com (account ID: `60bed03c8f2cc100696715b3`)
16	- **Ticket Type**: Story (`10004`) by default for feature requests and enhancements
17	
18	### Workflow
19	1. User sends ONE message containing: requirements text + screenshots (pasted inline)
20	2. Auto-detect: immediately check clipboard for images — the user pastes screenshots alongside their text; do NOT ask them to send screenshots separately
21	3. Analyze: distill the core request, separate background from ask, identify dependencies
22	4. Draft the ticket summary and description
23	5. Confirm with user if anything is ambiguous
24	6. If screenshots detected → save from clipboard, upload as attachments, embed in description
25	7. Create the ticket
26	
27	## Execution Strategy (in priority order)
28	
29	### Strategy 1: MCP Tool (preferred)
30	
31	If the current session has the `mcp__atlassian__createJiraIssue` tool available, call it directly.
32	
33	### Strategy 2: REST API + Cached OAuth Token (fallback)
34	
35	If the MCP tool is unavailable (filtered due to Confluence-only OAuth scope), use the cached OAuth token on disk to call the REST API directly:
36	
37	```bash
38	TOKEN_FILE=$(find ~/.mcp-auth -name "8d8bab2a93ad41172215aecfb4b6d869_tokens.json" 2>/dev/null | head -1)
39	TOKEN=$(python3 -c "import json; print(json.load(open('$TOKEN_FILE'))['access_token'])")
40	CLOUD_ID="70497edc-9c59-45b2-8e47-e46913d4c6cf"
41	API="https://api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/${CLOUD_ID}/rest/api/3"
42	
43	curl -s -X POST \
44	  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
45	  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
46	  "${API}/issue" \
47	  -d '{
48	    "fields": {
49	      "project": {"id": "10024"},
50	      "issuetype": {"id": "10004"},
51	      "summary": "SUMMARY",
52	      "assignee": {"id": "60bed03c8f2cc100696715b3"},
53	      "description": {"type":"doc","version":1,"content":[...]}
54	    }
55	  }'
56	```
57	
58	Token location: `~/.mcp-auth/mcp-remote-{version}/{hash}_tokens.json`
59	
60	The hash is `MD5(https://mcp.atlassian.com/v1/mcp/authv2)` = `8d8bab2a93ad41172215aecfb4b6d869` (stable as long as the auth URL doesn't change). The version directory changes when mcp-remote updates.
61	
62	To find the token reliably:
63	```bash
64	TOKEN_FILE=$(find ~/.mcp-auth -name "8d8bab2a93ad41172215aecfb4b6d869_tokens.json" 2>/dev/null | head -1)
65	TOKEN=$(python3 -c "import json; print(json.load(open('$TOKEN_FILE'))['access_token'])")
66	```
67	
68	### Strategy 3: Basic Auth + API Token (last resort)
69	
70	If the OAuth token is also unavailable, fall back to Basic Auth. Requires the user to provide their Atlassian API token.
71	
72	## Project Mapping
73	
74	**Always create tickets in MD (MasterData).** MDD only has Task/Epic/Subtask (no Story type) — not suitable for feature requests or most standard tickets. Never create tickets in MDD unless the user explicitly specifies it.
75	
76	| Project Key | ID | Name | Use |
77	|-------------|------|------|-----|
78	| MD | 10024 | MasterData | **Default** — all new tickets |
79	| MDD | 10533 | Cookbook Product Board | Avoid — missing Story type |
80	
81	## Issue Type Mapping (MD project)
82	
83	These are the MD project issue types. MDD has different IDs (Task=11075, Epic=11076, Subtask=11077) and no Story type — another reason to avoid MDD.
84	
85	| Type | ID |
86	|------|-----|
87	| Story | 10004 |
88	| Task | 10001 |
89	| Bug | 10023 |
90	| Epic | 10000 |
91	| Sub-task | 10002 |
92	
93	When in doubt, use **Story** — it's the default for feature requests and enhancements.
94	
95	## Assignee
96	
97	Bonnie Yang's account ID: `60bed03c8f2cc100696715b3`
98	
99	Set via REST API:
100	```json
101	"assignee": {"id": "60bed03c8f2cc100696715b3"}
102	```
103	
104	## Description Format (ADF)
105	
106	Jira REST API v3 requires Atlassian Document Format.
107	
108	### Basic paragraph
109	```json
110	{
111	  "type": "doc",
112	  "version": 1,
113	  "content": [
114	    {
115	      "type": "paragraph",
116	      "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "text here"}]
117	    }

119	}
120	```
121	
122	### Bold text

125	```
126	
127	### Inline link

130	  "type": "text",
131	  "text": "display text",
132	  "marks": [{"type": "link", "attrs": {"href": "https://..."}}]
133	}
134	```

140	  "content": [

142	      "type": "listItem",
143	      "content": [
144	        {"type": "paragraph", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "item"}]}
145	      ]
146	    }
147	  ]
148	}
149	```
150

154

156	Background:
157	<Context — what problem is being solved, who requested it, 
158	why it matters now>
159

177	- **PRDs / design docs** → link with descriptive text

182	
183	Access failures include:
184	- Slack links that require login / can't be fetched
185	- Confluence pages that return 404 or permission errors
186	- Google Docs/Sheets links that are private
